total_unique_sources.note: De-duplication is by full URL. Same URL cited in multiple stages counts once. Vendor auto-low sources counted in their own bucket.
total_unique_sources.methodology: Sourced from the 42 unique source catalogs logged in per-stage JSONs. Estimated via domain-pair deduplication across all 6 stages.
total_unique_sources.diversity_assessment: 148 unique URLs across 6 stages is within the IMI 40-60 URL target for a single stage but well exceeds it for a 6-stage corpus. Corpus-level source diversity is structurally adequate in count but severely skewed: 29 auto-low vendor URLs (20% of total) and 8 aggregator-market-research URLs (5%) pull in the wrong direction. The 67 primary-academic sources are the strongest category but are predominantly single-citation (no claim in any stage reaches High via academic sources alone because the rubric requires 3+ for High without a gov/multilateral). Only 5 primary-gov and 9 primary-ministry sources appear across the entire 6-stage corpus — a structural weakness for a research programme focused on heavily regulated healthcare markets in Indonesia and Malaysia where BPS, DOSM, Kemenkes, MOH Malaysia, BPJS Kesehatan, and OJK all publish directly relevant primary statistics.

source_overlap_observations.claim_anchored: Only 32% of 273 assessed FKTPs met Level 4 RPPT target by December 2023
source_overlap_observations.issue: This is the single most important quantitative claim in the corpus — the foundation of the CDM recall failure case across PP2.2 and PP6.1. It is cited in two stages but only from a single URL (BPJS Kesehatan Journal). Cross-stage repetition does not create a second independent source. The claim remains Low in both stages due to single-source override. A corroborating BPJS Kesehatan annual report PDF or Kemenkes monitoring publication is the single highest-leverage gap in the entire corpus.

The same two job-aggregator URLs — JobStreet Indonesia GP salary and Indeed Malaysia nurse salary — are used as the labor cost anchor across all 6 stages. Both are (a) secondary-trade, (b) frequently cited for occupational categories other than what is being measured (the GP URL is used for admin salary, the nurse URL is used for admin salary), and (c) single-source. The effect is that every labor cost model in the corpus compounds the same two weak salary references into different cost equations. A single BPS Indonesia Sakernas wage table and a single DOSM Malaysia Salaries and Wages Survey entry would simultaneously upgrade cost anchors in all 6 stages.

source_overlap_observations.claim_anchored: Manual data entry generates 3-5% error rate at $45-65/incident; $150K/year admin burden for multi-provider US clinic
source_overlap_observations.issue: A single US industry blog (rovinghealth.com) provides the transcription error rate and rework cost cited in both Stage 2 (PP2.1) and Stage 3 (PP3.1). Trade-press-only override applies to operating cost figures. Citing the same blog twice across two stages does not increase source independence — it remains one source family. A JAMIA, BMC Health Services Research, or similar peer-reviewed study on healthcare data entry error rates is needed.

source_overlap_observations.claim_anchored: Indonesia health check-up market USD 656M (2024), 9.9% CAGR; Malaysia health check-up market USD 283.8M (2024), 10.8% CAGR
source_overlap_observations.issue: The entire MCU market sizing for both countries rests on Grand View Research, a private aggregator subject to the auto-low-aggregator override. The same two URLs appear in Stage 3 and again in Stage 4's market context table without any primary-tier cross-validation in either stage. No World Bank health expenditure data, ADB health sector assessment, IFC private health market study, or national health accounts statistic corroborates these figures.

source_overlap_observations.claim_anchored: 67% of Malaysian hospital specialists report GLs revoked; 83% rate TPA clinical competency as 'little or no understanding'; 99% perceive insurer interference; 73% report patients experienced delayed treatment
source_overlap_observations.issue: The CodeBlue October 2025 specialist poll (n=855) is cited in Stage 1 (PP1.3) and cited no fewer than 6 times across different claims in Stage 5 (PP5.1, PP5.3). This single survey, run and published by CodeBlue trade press with no independent peer review of methodology, carries essentially the entire evidentiary weight for the Malaysian specialist-TPA conflict pain point. Single-source override applies to every individual claim. The volume of cross-claim repetition is a red flag for downstream readers who might mistake citation frequency for source independence.

source_overlap_observations.claim_anchored: PROLANIS scoping review 2025: East Java 34.3% of eligible enrolled, 56.8% regular attendance, WhatsApp non-participation and supply barriers as recall failure modes
source_overlap_observations.issue: This is a legitimate primary-academic source cited appropriately in both Stage 2 and Stage 6. Cross-citation is noted but does not create an issue — the scoping review is directly relevant to both stages. However, treating cross-stage citations of the same PMC source as independent evidence in a composite score would be an error; each stage must demonstrate independent corroboration.

source_overlap_observations.claim_anchored: Permata Cibubur Hospital IS evaluation 2025: MCU results still in printed physical documents; LIS integration not achieved
source_overlap_observations.issue: Single primary-academic source (Permata Cibubur 2025 evaluation) cited in both Stage 3 and Stage 4 as structural evidence for manual MCU operations. This is a single-facility study at one Indonesian hospital — cited as the primary published evidence of MCU manual operations across both stages. Khazanah Sosial 2025 (also cited) covers a different hospital, which together provide two case examples; neither is a national survey or representative sample.

29 auto-low vendor sources appear across the 6-stage corpus. Notably, Prodia OHI (prodia.co.id + prodiaohi.co.id) is cited 4-5 times across Stages 3 and 4 as evidence for Prodia's own scale (>500,000 employees/year, >2,000 companies). The '500,000 employees' figure, which is used repeatedly to scale the MCU collation pain point, is unverified by any audited filing or independent third-party confirmation. In Indonesia, Prodia (PT Prodia Widyahusada Tbk) is a listed company on IDX — its 20-F equivalent (annual report) would provide audited revenue and service volume data that would immediately replace the marketing-page citations.

source_overlap_observations.claim_anchored: Indonesia BPJS Kesehatan spends >IDR 30.5 trillion ($1.88B) annually on DM and HT management; FKTP CDM utilization rates
source_overlap_observations.issue: A single paywalled Kompas.id article is cited in both Stage 2 (PP2.1 and PP2.2) and Stage 4 (PP4.4) for the BPJS DM+HT total expenditure figure and CDM utilization gap. The article is tagged [NEEDS-ATTENDED-FETCH] and cannot be directly verified. Cross-stage citation of an unverifiable paywall source does not improve evidentiary standing. BPJS Kesehatan publishes official data on program expenditure in its annual report (laporan tahunan) which would replace this citation.

source_overlap_observations.note: ASSUMED-tagged claims appear in every stage: Stage 1 (7 tagged), Stage 2 (8 tagged), Stage 3 (8 tagged), Stage 4 (7 tagged), Stage 5 (5 tagged), Stage 6 (11 tagged). Total: 46 explicitly assumed claims across the corpus. These are appropriately flagged and do not inflate confidence scores, but they signal that all willingness-to-pay figures, labor time benchmarks, and operating cost model inputs remain unvalidated by primary data in all 6 stages. No primary interview transcript, no time-motion study, and no WTP survey result appears in any stage's footnotes.

corpus_confidence_rollup.source_of_scores: Per-stage JSON files: pass-2-validation/stage-{1-6}.json. Stage 1 scores are pre-deep-research (pass-3 outcomes not yet reflected in a revised stage-1.json). Stages 2-6 scores are as-filed at pass-2.
corpus_confidence_rollup.note_on_stage_1_post_dr: Stage 1's pass-3 deep research targeted 6 weak claims. If those 6 claims each upgraded by 1 tier on average (Low → Medium or Medium → High), the corpus total would shift by approximately 6 claims, bringing Low to ~247/300 (82.3%) — still well above the 70% re-run-recommended threshold. Even an optimistic scenario where all 6 Stage 1 claims upgraded to High would move the Low% to 80.7%. The gate decision does not change.

gate_reasoning: The corpus-level Low confidence percentage is 84.3% (253 of 300 claims scored Low), far above the 70% re-run-recommended threshold. This is not a borderline case. Even accounting for Stage 1's pass-3 deep-research improvements (not yet scored in a revised JSON), the Low percentage cannot drop below 80% without a substantial multi-stage deep-research pass. The structural root causes are: (1) across all 6 stages, nearly every quantitative claim — patient volumes, labor times, error rates, market sizes, salary benchmarks, follow-up compliance rates, no-show rates — rests on a single source or an assumed tag, making single-source override the dominant driver of Low scores; (2) salary data across all 6 stages routes through the same two job-aggregator URLs (JobStreet Indonesia GP salary, Indeed Malaysia nurse salary) rather than BPS Sakernas or DOSM wage surveys; (3) market sizing in Stages 3 and 4 depends entirely on Grand View Research (auto-low-aggregator); (4) Stage 5's TPA/insurer stage (62 claims, 98.4% Low) is structurally the weakest, with the CodeBlue n=855 specialist survey cited 10+ times as the sole source for all specialist-TPA conflict claims, and an AI vendor's own blog (InterPixels AI) as the sole source for the 60-75% auto-adjudication rate claim that anchors all medical review queue sizing; (5) 29 auto-low-vendor citations appear across the corpus for vendor scale and product claims with no audited filing corroboration — notably Prodia OHI's '500,000 employees/year' figure (cited as primary evidence of MCU market scale in Stages 3 and 4) comes only from Prodia's own marketing pages rather than its IDX-listed annual report. Stages 2 and 3 are closest to a ship-with-flag threshold individually (67.6% and 56.7% Low respectively), and the underlying structural narrative across all 6 stages is coherent and directionally credible — the pain points are real and the evidence direction is correct. However, the cost models, frequency claims, and supporting benchmarks need primary-tier sourcing before the corpus can support a sourced business case.

vertical_slice_notes: The IMI vertical slice diversity check assesses whether the full 6-stage corpus demonstrates adequate source category diversity — that is, that the research programme has reached primary government/multilateral/ministry sources, not just academic and trade sources. Across 148 unique URLs, only 5 primary-gov and 9 primary-ministry sources appear (9% of total unique sources). Specifically missing across the entire corpus: (1) No BPS Indonesia wage or health facility data cited with correct URL and access confirmation outside of Stage 1 post-DR partial fix. (2) No DOSM Malaysia labour or health statistics cited at all. (3) No ADB, World Bank, or OECD health financing data cited for market sizing corroboration. (4) No BPJS Kesehatan official annual report or monthly performance publication directly cited (only news reporting of BPJS data). (5) No BNM Malaysia Insurance Annual Statistics cited to cross-validate TPA market figures. (6) No MOH Malaysia Health Facts or Annual Report directly cited for market sizing (Stage 1 uses MOH Health Facts 2024 for clinic count — the only clear primary-ministry success). The vertical slice requires that at least the top-3 pain points per stage can be anchored to at least one primary-gov, primary-ministry, or primary-multilateral source. No stage achieves this except partially in Stage 1 (Kemenkes clinic count) and Stage 2 (BPJS Kesehatan Journal for RPPT data). Diversity check: FAIL.
